opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Christ already did what we keep trying to do.

His mercy endures forever. He lived for us and He died for us. That part is finished. The sacrifice has been made.
“For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.”

So now the question is not how we become perfect. That has already been taken care of. The question is whether we accept it.

We spend so much time chasing perfection, chasing control, chasing worth. But He already fulfilled it.
“Therefore let us celebrate the feast, not with the old yeast, the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.”

He did the hard part.

Now we are asked to live in it.
To live in His joy.
To live in His mercy.

Not ignoring sin—but not being consumed by it either. We are human. We will fall. That is not new. What is new is that we are no longer defined by it.

So the call is not “go be perfect.”
The call is: go love.
Love Him. Love others. Let go of the old yeast.

We look to His right hand, not to this world. We follow in obedience and faith, not in fear.

And in that, something shifts.
There is a kind of rest that comes—not at the end of life, but now. A quiet knowing that we belong to Him, and that we will be revealed with Him.

“Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into His glory?”

We see that glory every Sunday. In the breaking of the bread. In the Eucharist. He is still giving Himself to us.

We make this so much harder than it is.

God has already made the way.
We have already been given everything in Jesus.

So stop striving like it depends on you.
Be still. Receive. And then live it.

He died for us.
We are made new in Him.
